stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs sold through 7 of 8 crashes even as Wall Street tames BTC selloffs
stories.summary: An analysis found spot bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows during seven of the last eight major bitcoin price crashes, meaning ETF holders kept selling under stress rather than holding firm. At the same time, growing Wall Street participation appears to be making BTC selloffs less violent overall. The findings cut against the idea that ETF adoption alone stabilizes price during downturns.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flow behavior during crashes is a key test of whether institutional adoption reduces or amplifies bitcoin's volatility.
whatToWatch: How ETF flows behave in the next major bitcoin drawdown
Whether outflow patterns shift as the ETF holder base matures
questions: What was different about the one crash where ETFs didn't sell?
Are the outflows concentrated among a few large holders or broad-based?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs sold through 7 of 8 crashes even as Wall Street makes BTC selloffs less violent

stories.title: Robinhood earns $51 million in blockchain fees while Ethereum settlement costs just $69,000
stories.summary: Robinhood generated roughly $51 million in blockchain-related fees, while the underlying Ethereum network settlement costs for that activity totaled only about $69,000, according to CryptoSlate. The gap shows most of the fee revenue around crypto trading goes to intermediaries, not the base-layer network processing the transactions.
stories.whyItMatters: The disparity shows where value capture actually happens in crypto trading infrastructure, relevant to anyone assessing fee economics across exchanges and layer-1 networks.
whatToWatch: Whether other brokerages show a similar gap between fees charged and on-chain costs
Any response from Robinhood on its fee structure
questions: What specific services make up the $51 million in fees?
Does this reflect Robinhood's product mix or a broader industry pattern?

sources.title: Robinhood generates $51 million in blockchain fees while Ethereum settlement costs total just $69,000

stories.title: Midnight privacy-vault demo needs outside signers to release Ethereum tokens
stories.summary: A demonstration of a privacy vault on the Midnight network reportedly needs external signers to approve the release of Ethereum tokens, rather than relying only on the vault's own cryptographic design. CryptoSlate's report flags this as a trust dependency built into the current demo.
stories.whyItMatters: A privacy tool that depends on outside signers raises questions about how decentralized and trust-minimized it actually is.
whatToWatch: Whether Midnight removes the signer dependency before a wider release
Community scrutiny of the vault's security model
questions: Who are the outside signers and how are they chosen?
Is this a demo-only limitation or part of the permanent design?

sources.title: A Midnight privacy-vault demo needs outside signers to release Ethereum tokens

stories.title: OCC drops proposed affiliate-rewards presumption but keeps stablecoin yield ban
stories.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency withdrew a proposed presumption on affiliate rewards programs, but left its existing ban on stablecoin yield in place, per CryptoSlate. The move narrows one part of the regulator's proposal while keeping the restriction crypto firms have objected to.
stories.whyItMatters: The stablecoin yield ban directly affects whether issuers and partner banks can offer interest-bearing stablecoin products in the US.
whatToWatch: Industry reaction to the remaining yield ban
Any further OCC rulemaking on bank-crypto partnerships
questions: Why did the OCC drop the affiliate-rewards presumption specifically?
Could the yield ban still be revised or challenged?

sources.title: OCC drops proposed affiliate rewards presumption, but stablecoin yield ban stays

stories.title: Standard Chartered brings crypto custody in-house amid Wall Street infrastructure race
stories.summary: Standard Chartered is moving to bring its crypto custody operations in-house, according to CryptoSlate, as traditional banks compete to build out digital-asset infrastructure. The shift points toward direct control of client crypto holdings rather than reliance on third-party custodians.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank internalizing crypto custody signals institutional adoption is moving from pilot projects into core infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Timeline for Standard Chartered's in-house custody rollout
Whether other banks announce similar moves
questions: Which third-party custodian, if any, does this replace?
Which client segments will the in-house custody serve first?

sources.title: Standard Chartered moves to bring crypto custody in-house as Wall Street’s digital asset infrastructure race accelerates

stories.title: Bitcoin Core 32 bug can stall multisig signing on older nodes; fix delayed
stories.summary: A bug in Bitcoin Core version 32 can stall multisig transaction signing on older nodes, and the fix has slipped to a future patch instead of shipping immediately, per CryptoSlate. Users running the affected node versions remain exposed to the signing issue until the patch lands.
stories.whyItMatters: Multisig setups secure large bitcoin holdings for exchanges and custodians, so a signing bug affects custody security and operations across the ecosystem.
whatToWatch: Release timing for the patch that fixes the bug
Guidance from Bitcoin Core maintainers for affected node operators in the meantime
questions: How many nodes or wallets are actually affected?
Is there a workaround for multisig signing until the patch ships?

sources.title: Bitcoin Core 32 can stall multisig signing on older nodes as fix slips to next patch

stories.title: Solana bot turns $12,000 into $1.4 billion in volume as fake liquidity floods Raydium
stories.summary: A trading bot on Solana reportedly generated $1.4 billion in trading volume from just $12,000 in starting capital, flooding the Raydium decentralized exchange with what CryptoSlate describes as fake liquidity. The pattern points to wash-trading-style volume inflation rather than genuine market demand.
stories.whyItMatters: Inflated DEX volume can mislead traders about real liquidity and distort token rankings or incentive programs tied to volume metrics.
whatToWatch: Whether Raydium or the Solana ecosystem takes action against the bot
Any broader look into wash trading on Solana DEXs
questions: Is this activity illegal or just exploiting incentive mechanics?
How widespread is similar bot activity on other Solana DEXs?

sources.title: Solana bot turns just $12,000 into $1.4 billion in trading volume as fake liquidity floods Raydium

stories.title: Railway urges credential resets after investigator alleges $371,000 crypto theft
stories.summary: Cloud hosting platform Railway is urging users to reset credentials after an investigator alleged a theft of about $371,000 in crypto tied to the platform, according to CryptoSlate. The exact attack method wasn't detailed beyond the credential-reset guidance.
stories.whyItMatters: The incident shows crypto theft increasingly exploits developer infrastructure and hosting platforms, not just exchange hacks.
whatToWatch: Railway's official incident response and findings
Whether affected users recover funds or face further exposure
questions: How were the credentials initially compromised?
Is this an isolated incident or part of a broader campaign?

sources.title: Railway urges credential resets as investigator alleges $371,000 crypto theft

stories.title: Binance to exclude disrupted overnight data from stock-futures funding calculations
stories.summary: Binance is adjusting how it calculates funding rates for its stock-related futures products by excluding data from periods of overnight disruption, per CryptoSlate. The change is meant to stop abnormal or interrupted data feeds from skewing funding rates on these products.
stories.whyItMatters: Funding-rate calculations directly affect trader costs and returns on leveraged futures positions, so changes to the methodology matter operationally.
whatToWatch: How Binance defines and detects future data disruptions
Trader reaction to the revised funding methodology
questions: What specific disruption prompted this change?
Will other exchanges offering similar products adopt the same approach?

sources.title: Binance moves to exclude disrupted overnight data from stock-futures funding

stories.title: Qubic's recovery rules require ownership checks even for unstolen funds in vulnerable wallets
stories.summary: Qubic has set recovery rules that require ownership verification even for funds that weren't stolen but sit in wallets identified as vulnerable, according to CryptoSlate. The policy applies broadly to at-risk wallets rather than only to confirmed theft cases.
stories.whyItMatters: How a protocol handles recovery for vulnerable-but-unstolen funds sets a precedent for balancing security intervention against user custody rights.
whatToWatch: Response from wallet holders subject to the ownership checks
Whether other chains adopt similar vulnerability-based recovery policies
questions: What makes a wallet count as "vulnerable" under Qubic's criteria?
Could ownership checks be used to freeze funds without clear evidence of theft?

sources.title: Qubic’s recovery rules require ownership checks even for unstolen funds in vulnerable wallets
